articles.title: What are Family Accounts?
articles.body:
A quick guide to Family Accounts


When you set up a player to get it online and pair it with the phone you are using for the Yoto app, you automatically create what we call a ‘Family Account’. 


A Family Account can be just one member and one player, or you could add more players and multiple members to the same account.



A Family Account lets anyone who is a member use the Yoto app to:

Control your player/s
Use the app to play content, adjust the volume, set a sleep timer etc. for any players in the Family Account

Manage player settings
Control features behind the scenes, like setting sleep and wake times, customizing the color of the nightlight and setting maximum volume.

Access cards you buy from Yoto instantly
When you purchase cards from the Yoto Store (using the same email address as you use for the app) those cards will be added to your Library straight away, so you can enjoy listening to them before the actual cards arrive in the post

articles.title: How to add users to your Family Account
articles.body:
Set up your player so that more than one person can be linked to the same account.


Adding a user to a Family Account

If a partner has already set up your player, got it online and has paired it, this will have set up a Family Account. When you join this Family Account, both of you will be able to see and play all the cards your family owns, as well as manage player settings.


To join an existing Family Account

1. Make sure you are signed in to the app with your own email address 

2. Go to the Menu screen in the app and tap ‘Join a Family Account’


This will take you through a shortened version of the set-up flow (you won’t need to enter Wi-Fi details to get the player online)

Note: you’ll need to enter the six letter security code generated on the front of the player, so you will need to have access to the player itself 


3. When prompted, tap ‘Join This Family Account’

Success!

Once you have joined a Family Account as the second user, you will see your own details (and the details of any other paired users) at the top of the Players tab in the app.

You will also be able to access settings for each player in your account. From here you can manage settings and personalise features, such as bedtime/wake time and set the color of the nightlight (on Yoto Player (3rd Generation). 

Note: a user account can only be part of one Family Account. If a user joins a Family Account while already being in another Family Account, they will automatically leave their previous Family Account and join the new one. 


How to change the account owner

The account owner is the lead grown-up for the Family Account and can manage all other account members and users.

To make another family member the account owner:

  1. Open the Yoto App and go to Settings.
  2. Find the family member at the top of the screen.
  3. Tap the three dots next to their email address.
  4. Tap Make account owner and follow the prompts to confirm.

The selected family member will then become the account owner.

articles.title: How to add Yoto players to your Family Account
articles.body:
How to add a second or more Yoto players to your Family Account.


If you own more than one player, you can set them up in the same Family Account!


Benefits of adding a second player to your Family Account

If you have had your player for a while, you will know the benefits of Family Accounts, and how they allow more than one parent to manage settings on the player, as well as see and play all of a family's audio content directly from the phone.

If you own more than one player, you can add all of your players to the same Family Account. This lets you manage them from a single screen in the Yoto app with a single login (per user).


How to add a second player to your Family Account

You can set up a second player and join it to your Family Account as part of the Set Up a Player process.


To pair your phone and join the player to your family account, simply tap the Pair My Phone button.


What your account will look like in the app

Once you have set up your second player in your Family Account, you will be able to see it in the Settings tab in the app, as well as details of all paired users and any other players.

You will also be able to access the settings pages for each Yoto player in your account, in order to manage settings and personalise features such as bedtime/wake time and the setting of the color of the nightlight (on Yoto Players (3rd Generation)).

If you need help, don't hesitate to contact us!

articles.body:
Each member of a Family Account can either remove themselves or remove other users.
To remove a user from a Family Account:

  • Open the Yoto App
  • Go to the Settings tab

articles.title: Account FAQs
articles.body:
Why do I need an account?

We require customers to create an account so that we can ensure any Yoto Cards that you have purchased are correctly added to your account, meaning you can access them from your Yoto App's card library.

Rest assured that we keep your information safe and never share it with anyone else, but we do use 3rd party programs in order to keep your information safe. 

Click here to read our full privacy policy (link opens in a new tab).


How do I create and access my Yoto account?

You can sign up and log into your account from our website, yotoplay.com, using the button in the shape of a person, found in the top-right corner. It's the one between the search icon and the wishlist.


You can also create an account from the Yoto App, before log in.

If you have forgotten your password, click on Login, and select the Forgot your password? option. Remember to check your spam folder for the password reset email!

Note: becoming a Yoto Club member does not automatically create an account. You will need to use the same email address that you used to purchase your Club membership to also create an account on our website.


Can I change my account's email address?

The email address of your Yoto account cannot be changed.

If you have lost access to your old email address, please create a new Yoto account. By adding your new Yoto account to the Family Account, you will retain access to your devices and library.

The order history, wishlist, saved address, and Yoto Club subscriptions, however, cannot be moved—but we will do our best to help you close down the old account.


How do I delete my account?

To delete your account: 

  • Open the Yoto App
  • Go to the Settings tab
  • Tap the three dots menu next to a user 
  • This will show the menu with the remove options
  • Select "Delete my Yoto app account" 

Note: if you inadvertently delete your account, contact us, and we may be able to reinstate it.

articles.title: I can't log in to my Yoto account
articles.body:
Common log-in issues.

If you're not able to log in to your Yoto account and are not receiving a password reset email when requested, here are some things to try. You'd be surprised how often these work!

  • Make sure you're using the email that you signed up with: you can check this in the Settings tab of your Yoto App.
  • Check for typos in your email or password. We've all typed .con instead of .com sometime!
  • Check your spam folder or other folders of your inbox. The password reset email may be waiting for you.
  • Try to Sign up instead of Log in. Sometimes the log in doesn't work because the account doesn't exist yet. 


Too many log in attempts

If too many log in attempts are unsuccessful, the account will be temporarily blocked for its safety. If this happens, don't worry! Just get in touch and we'll unblock it for you.


Removing an email address

If the original email address you used is incorrect or not in use any more, and you wish to remove it from your Family account: 

  • Go to the Settings section of the app
  • Tap the three dots menu next to the email address you wish to remove  
  • Tap Leave this family account

articles.title: How to refer a friend to Yoto
articles.body:
Sharing Yoto with friends is a simple way to spread the joy of audio, and earn a little reward for yourself along the way!


What’s new

Our updated Refer a Friend program is live, more rewarding than ever, offering: 

  • A discount for your friend on their first Yoto Player or Yoto Mini purchase
  • A Reward Voucher for you after your friend’s order ships


Discount and Reward values 

Referral values vary by region and the Yoto store you shop from. They are shown clearly at the time of redemption.

Regional storeUKUSCAAUEUFR
Friend DiscountOutside Promotions£15$20$20$30€15€15
During Promotions £5$5$5$10€5€5
Reward Voucher (Referrer)£15$20$20$30€15€15



How it works


  1. Share your referral link 
  • Look out for a Refer a Friend button or link. You might find it:
    • On yotoplay.com (in the website footer or after checkout on the thank you page)
    • In your account dashboard (My Account → Refer a Friend)
    • In the Yoto app (Library tab → tap the gift icon in the top-right corner)


    • In emails from us, such as order confirmations or newsletters

  • Enter your email to get your unique referral link 
    • You don’t need a Yoto account to refer a friend, just an email address!
    • Once you enter your email, your unique referral link will be generated.
    • ⚠️ Your rewards will be linked to that email address, so make sure it’s one you’ll continue to use. 
  • Share your link
    • Copy your referral link and share it with friends, family, or colleagues, anyone you know who’d love Yoto.
    • ⚠️ Referral links are for personal sharing only. They shouldn’t be posted publicly (for example on social media, forums, deal or coupon websites, or shared in bulk). Publicly shared links may be disabled, and rewards may not be issued.


    2. Your friend unlocks their discount 

  • Your friend clicks your referral link and enters their email address 
    • This will generate a referral discount code.
  • The referral discount applies when the order includes a Yoto Player or a Yoto Mini
    • Cards and accessories can be added to the same order, but the discount requires a Player or Mini to be in the basket.
  • The discount code will: 
    • appear automatically at checkout, 
    • or your friend can copy and paste the code manually once it’s generated. 
    • They will receive it via email as well. 
    • ⚠️ Your friend must use the same email address at checkout as the one they entered when generating the referral code. If a different email is used, the discount won’t apply and the referral can’t be tracked.


    3. Your Reward Voucher is issued 

  • Once your friend’s order ships, your reward voucher will be sent by email within 7 days.
  • You can use your reward voucher on most items in the Yoto store, including Players, cards, accessories, and so much more!
  • However, reward vouchers cannot be used on:
    • Yoto Club subscriptions
    • Orders using Club Credits
  • Your voucher will be valid for 6 months. 



A few handy details 

  • Each friend can only be referred once.
  • As a Referrer, you can earn rewards for up to 10 successful referrals per year. The cap will reset once you reach 10 referrals.
  • Friend referral discount applies only to the purchase of a Yoto Player or a Yoto Mini. 
  • Referral links are for personal sharing only and shouldn’t be posted publicly.
  • Here's how referral rewards interact with Yoto Club benefits: 
    • ✅ Referral reward vouchers (for you, the Referrer) can be combined with the Yoto Club 10% member discount
    • ❌ Referral reward vouchers (for you, the Referrer)  can’t be used on orders that include Yoto Club Credits, even if credits are only used for part of the order
    • ❌ Friend referral discounts (for the person you refer) don’t combine with Yoto Club benefits, including: Yoto Club 10% member discount and the usage of Yoto 

Referral Booster: Limited-time reward boost 🎉

We’re giving our Refer a Friend programme a little extra sparkle!

A Referral Booster is live across all regions from 6 February (8:30am GMT) until 18 February. During this time, the referrer reward is boosted, meaning you’ll earn a bigger thank-you when a friend successfully uses your referral link.


What’s boosted?

  • ✅ Referrer reward only (the person sharing the link)
  • ❌ Your friend’s discount stays the same


Important things to know

  • The booster is live since 6 February at 8:30am GMT
  • No retroactive rewards apply
    If you referred a friend before the booster started and already received the standard reward, it can’t be increased
  • You can still earn the boosted reward by referring new friends who are new to the referral programme

articles.title: Third-party developers and your account data
articles.body:
Yoto is an open platform, blessed with a wonderfully creative community, and we believe that enabling independent developers to build on it makes the product better for everyone.

We are proud to have a community of developers that make useful, fun and interesting apps on top of the Yoto platform for you all to enjoy.


What kind of data can a third party developer access?

When you press “Log in with Yoto” you're (at minimum) giving the third party basic access to your Yoto profile data. This means your:

  • email address
  • country
  • name that you provided
  • unique user ID

On top of that, apps will need to access different parts of your Yoto data depending on their functionality.


Further data examples

For example, let's look at an app that monitors the battery of your Yoto devices and then sends you an email or text when any of them needs charging.

It always needs access to your Yoto devices because that's how it knows what their battery levels are, and can then send you an email to notify you. But that app doesn't need access to your playlists. And it might be suspicious if it did.

An app like a playlist editor, on the other hand, needs access to your playlists and content library so it can help you create, edit and manage your own cards. But it wouldn’t need access to your device battery status or usage data.

We always recommend checking what permissions an app is requesting and making sure they match what the app is supposed to do.


How can I revoke access given to a third party?

You’re always in control of which apps can access your Yoto account.

If you no longer want to use a third-party app, you can revoke its access at any time by contacting us.

Once access is removed, that app will no longer have direct access to your Yoto data.

Note that this doesn’t affect any data the app developer already has. If you want these removed it’s best to contact the developer directly.

If you ever log in to the app in the future, you’ll be asked to grant permissions again, and have an opportunity to review exactly what access it’s requesting before continuing.


What can I do if I'm worried about a third party app or developer?

The best way is to contact the developer directly. So far we found that developers have been very willing to engage with their users and try to make the experience better for everyone.

If you're experiencing negative behaviour or something else that you feel like is against Yoto’s Creator Guidelines then you can report it to us by sending an email to developers@yotoplay.com.


What is an unverified app?

An unverified app is one that hasn't been through Yoto's review process.

You'll see a warning on the login screen letting you know when this is the case, and you'll need to explicitly accept before continuing.

Think of it like any other website or app you come across on the internet, it's worth taking a moment to check who made it, what it does, and whether you're comfortable with what it's asking for before giving it access to your Yoto account.


How does Yoto verify published apps?

We review every app before it's listed on our official channels (like the Yoto App or Yoto Space). This includes checking for security issues, ensuring compliance with our content guidelines, and verifying that the developer has provided adequate information.

We also confirm that apps do what they claim without requesting excessive access to data, and that a clear privacy policy is in place.

Despite all of this, it’s still important for you to choose which ones you trust based on your level of comfort with what you’re willing to share.

articles.title: Joining the Yoto Beta programme
articles.body:
Yoto Beta gives you a chance to preview new features coming to Yoto ahead of general release.


To share your feedback, suggestions or report any issues, please email us at beta@yotoplay.com.

Please note that when you sign up for Beta, you do so for each product individually.


Yoto OS Beta

You can enrol your Player into Yoto OS Beta in Yoto App by navigating to Player Settings → Yoto Beta Labs section. (You don't need Yoto App Beta)

When you join the Beta, please allow your Yoto player a few minutes online and idle, so it can update its firmware to the latest version.

Please bear in mind that Beta rollouts are gradual, so your Player may take an additional day or two to update.

Note: Devices which are running Yoto OS v2.23.3 are from the latest production batch of devices, and unfortunately these are not eligible for the beta program. We plan to resolve this in a subsequent beta version soon.

articles.title: Yoto App updates
articles.body:
See the features for the latest update we have made to the Yoto app, as well as all the previous updates.


Tip: you can check which version of the Yoto app you have by going to the Menu tab (in the app) where it is listed at  the bottom of the screen. 


Yoto app updates

We release updates for the app regularly, bringing in new features, optimising performance and squishing bugs that come along from time to time. It's probably a good idea to switch on auto updates for the app, if you don't have this already.


Yoto app reviews

We really appreciate your app reviews and feedback. If you love our updates, please do leave a review in the app stores.

iPhone: https://apps.apple.com/app/yoto-music-stories-learning/id1412039719

Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.yotoplay.yoto


Yoto app (Beta)

We make an app beta available for external testing before we promote the new release to the app stores. Whilst we test extensively and endeavour to ensure the app operates in beta without issues, there are times when glitches may arise. Participating in the app beta gives you access to new features ahead of time but with the caveat that there may be glitches that we haven't spotted. If you let us know at hello@yotoplay.com we can quickly put it right. To participate in the Yoto app beta, you can sign up via one of these links:

iPhone: https://testflight.apple.com/join/di4bwD5z

Android: https://play.google.com/apps/testing/com.yotoplay.yoto

articles.title: Using your Yoto as a Bluetooth speaker
articles.body:
Yoto Player (3rd Generation), Yoto Mini (2024 Edition) and Yoto Mini (2021–2023 Edition) can double as a Bluetooth speaker - pair your phone and play anything through your Yoto.


Please note: Bluetooth speaker functionality won't be available on 4th Generation Yoto Player or Yoto Mini at launch.  The good news is that it will be available at a later date. Like every Yoto before it, 4th Generation is designed to get better over time. Over-the-air updates mean your player will keep improving throughout its life - new features, refinements, and functionality added long after it arrives in your home. Bluetooth speaker is on that roadmap. 


For the latest information about Bluetooth speaker mode and other new features, see 4th Generation feature updates.



1. Switch Bluetooth on in the app

In the Yoto App, go to Settings and select your player. 

Scroll to the Advanced section at the bottom, and toggle Bluetooth Pairing on.

 

2. Put your player in pairing mode

Press and hold the left-hand orange button for about 3 seconds - a grey Bluetooth icon appears on the display.

Your player has two Bluetooth modes: one for headphones, one for speaker. Switch between them by rotating the Right hand button. 

With the speaker icon showing, press the right-hand orange button to choose it.


3. Pair from your phone

On your phone (or tablet), open Bluetooth settings and pair with your Yoto - just like any other Bluetooth speaker. When it connects, you’ll see a confirmation icon on your player’s display. Short-press the right-hand button, and you’re all set.

4. Play your audio

Anything playing on your phone now comes out of your Yoto. One thing to know: in speaker mode, control playback from your phone - the player’s buttons take a break.

 

5. Exit Bluetooth Mode

Press and hold the left-hand orange button for about 3 seconds - your player pops back to normal play mode, ready for cards.



Related help: Using headphones with your Yoto player.

articles.title: Using headphones with your Yoto player
articles.body:
Most Yoto players work with both wired and Bluetooth headphones - perfect for planes, car journeys and shared bedrooms. 

Check your model first, then follow the pairing steps for it.

Not sure which device you own? See: Which Yoto do I have?

Pairing Bluetooth headphones – 4th Generation players

  1. Keep your headphones close to the player, switch them on and put them in pairing mode. With the clock showing on your Yoto, press and hold the left-hand orange dial. A Bluetooth symbol with headphones appears, your player is looking for your headphones.  Please note: You will need to ensure "bluetooth audio" setting is enabled before the left hand button pairing functionality works

  1. When you see the green tick with headphones, you’re paired! Audio now plays through the headphones instead of the speaker. The player will return to the Clock screen and a blue dot will remain in the top left hand corner of the display. That means connection is successful.


If you see headphones with an exclamation mark, pairing failed or timed out (or the menu was left before finishing). Put your headphones back into pairing mode and try again.

Changed your mind while pairing?

To stop searching for headphones and exit the Bluetooth menu, press and hold either orange dial. Your Yoto will return to the Clock screen.

Want your Yoto to forget headphones that are already paired?

  1. With the clock showing, press and hold the left-hand orange dial. Your Yoto will connect to the paired headphones and return to the Clock screen.

  2. Press and hold the left-hand orange dial again to re-enter the Bluetooth menu.

  3. Press and hold the right-hand orange dial to disconnect and forget the headphones.

You’ll need to pair the headphones again if you want to use them with your Yoto in future.

Prefer to use your player as a Bluetooth speaker? Bluetooth speaker functionality won't be available on 4th Generation Yoto Player or Yoto Mini at launch.  The good news is that it will be available at a later date. Like every Yoto before it, 4th Generation is designed to get better over time. Over-the-air updates mean your player will keep improving throughout its life - new features, refinements, and functionality added long after it arrives in your home. Bluetooth speaker is on that roadmap. 


For the latest information about Bluetooth speaker mode and other new features, see 4th Generation feature updates.



Pairing Bluetooth headphones – Yoto Player (3rd Generation) and earlier Yoto Mini models

  1. Keep your headphones close to the player, switch them on and put them in pairing mode, so they go looking for your player.

  2. On the player, press and hold the left-hand orange button for about 3 seconds until the Bluetooth speaker mode icon appears.

  3. Turn the right-hand button clockwise until the headphone icon shows, then press the right-hand button to start pairing. The Bluetooth icon flashes blue while it searches.

  4. Paired! The display icons turn full colour, and a blue pixel appears in the top-left corner of the clock - that’s your “Bluetooth is active” indicator. Audio now plays through the headphones.

If you decide to cancel the pairing: 

  1. Hold the left hand button for 3 seconds to return to Bluetooth menu mode. 

  2. Rotate the right hand button to switch to the headphone option.

  3. Press the right hand button to select the headphone option. 

  4. Press the left hand button to exit the Bluetooth pairing.


Prefer to use your player as a Bluetooth speaker? At step 3, press the right-hand button on the speaker icon instead - then pair with the player from your phone’s Bluetooth settings, like any other speaker.


Troubleshooting

  • Headphones won’t reconnect automatically: reconnect manually - press and hold the left button, turn the right-hand button to the headphone icon, and press.

  • Audio stuttering: disconnect the headphones, then reconnect the same way.

  • Headphones won’t pair: some headphones start on a different Bluetooth version - press their pairing button a second time and try again.

  • Paired with the wrong headphones: the player connects to whichever pairing device has the strongest signal - switch off or move other Bluetooth devices out of range and retry.

  • Headphone port not working (no audio, tested with more than one pair): please contact us

articles.title: How to use the sleep timer on your Yoto
articles.body:
The Sleep Timer feature is perfect for bedtimes, but it can be useful for other situations too!


To set your player to stop playing after a set time, simply follow these simple steps: 

1) Tap the “now playing” bar at the base of the screen to open the Maxi Player view.

2) Tap the ‘moon and stars’ icon at the top of the screen.

3) Set your time.

4) Once the timer has elapsed, your player will stop playing. 


Don’t worry if you’ve changed cards or played something different while the timer is running, it will keep running until it runs out, or until you set it to 'off'.

To set your sleep timer off, simply tap the moon and stars icon again and select ‘off’.

articles.title: How to set an alarm on your Yoto
articles.body:
Our alarms are perfect for wake-up time, time to go to school, bedtime, but they can be useful for other situations too!


To get started, you will need to have the 2.46 version of the Yoto app or above, and Yoto player OS 2.10.7 or above. To set an alarm, simply follow these steps:

1) Open the Yoto App

2) Go to the Settings tab 


3) Go to the player settings of the player where you want to play alarms from. Make sure your player is switched on and connected to the internet.

4) In your chosen player settings, go to Alarms > Set an alarm

5) Go to Add an alarm

6) Select your alarm time

Tap the time

Scroll to your preferred alarm time

7) Select which days you want this alarm to be active for. 

The default setting is for every day to be selected, if you want your alarm to go off on specific days, tap the ones that don't apply.

Selected days will show in red and are listed in text underneath 

If you wanted your alarm to only be active Mon-Fri, this is what it would look like

8) Choose a sound for your alarm

Select from our 7 alarm sounds, tap on each sound to have a 3-second preview on your phone.

9) Select your alarm volume

You can do this by using the +/- buttons or our volume slider 

Please note, the alarm volume will not exceed your day or night settings. For example, if you set the alarm volume to 16, but your maximum day volume is 10, the alarm will play at a volume of 10.

10) Want to know what the alarm sounds like on your player? Use the preview on player button and the alarm will play for 10 seconds.

If you want to change any of the settings you have selected, just go back and make adjustments

11) Once you are happy with your alarm, click Save alarm

12) Press cancel to stop the alarm from being saved.

13) The saved alarm is now visible in the alarms settings. 

You can have a maximum of 10 alarms per player.


From this screen, you will be able to see your alarm time and the days selected. 

Here is what multiple alarms will look like:


14) To edit an alarm, tap on the alarm that you would like to make changes to, make your changes and don't forget to save! 


Or cancel if you don't want your changes to be saved.

15) To disable or enable an alarm, tap on the slider to the right of the alarm you would like to disable or enable.



16) To delete an alarm, tap on the alarm you would like to delete, scroll to the bottom and press the delete button. 


17) Please make sure your player is switched on at the time of the alarm for it to play.

18) To stop your alarm, press any player button or go to the app to stop it like an ordinary card.

articles.title: How to use the volume limiter on your Yoto
articles.body:
Keep little ears safe and sound! With Yoto’s built-in volume limiter, you can set the perfect listening level. No more loud surprises, just happy listening!


Using the volume limiter

To adjust your volume limiter, simply follow these steps:

1) Open the Yoto App

2) Go to the Settings tab 


3) Go to the player settings of the player that you want to adjust the volume limit of. Make sure your player is switched on and connected to the internet

4) In your chosen player settings, find the 'Day Volume Limit' and the 'Night Volume Limit'. You can set a value for both times of the day


The maximum volume is 16, and the lowest volume is 0 (this will result in no sound at all).

Tip: did you know that you can also enable the Headphone Volume Limiter from your player's settings? Just scroll further down on the same page to find this option.

articles.title: How to charge your Yoto player
articles.body:

articles.title: Yoto battery guide: how long it lasts, and how to check it
articles.body:
Up to a full day of adventures on one charge. Exactly how long depends on your model and how it’s used - here’s what to expect:


Not sure which device you own? See: Which Yoto do I have?


Your model

Battery life (up to)*

Yoto Player (4th Generation)

16 hours

Yoto Player (3rd Generation)

16 hours

Yoto Player (2nd Generation)

16 hours

Yoto Mini (4th Generation)

16 hours

Yoto Mini (2024 Edition)

14 hours

Yoto Mini (2021–2023 Edition)

14 hours

*Testing conducted with Battery Saver set to 1 minute, display brightness at 100%, volume step 8 and audio playing for 6 hours, to represent normal usage patterns. Battery life varies by use, configuration and age.



What affects battery life?


Three things make the biggest difference:

  • Streaming vs downloaded audio - streaming (playing audio over Wi-Fi uses more battery than playing audio that’s already downloaded.

  • Display brightness - brighter settings use more battery.

  • Battery Saver settings - leaving Battery Saver off shortens playback time. You can change these settings in the Yoto App. 


Making the battery last longer


In the Yoto App, go to Settings, open your player’s page, and you’ll find the following settings: 

  • Switch on Battery Saver - the biggest single win. Choose how long the display stays on before switching off. Turning the display off when it isn’t needed can add several hours of battery life. You’ll find Battery Saver in the Advanced panel. Don’t worry: the display pops straight back on when a card goes in or a button is pressed (or turned).

  • Keep the Auto Power-Off timer enabled. It switches your Yoto off when it’s not being used, so an idle player won’t drain overnight.

  • Download before you go. Play each title once while your player is online, then leave the player switched on, charging and idle so the download can finish. Downloaded audio can play offline and uses less battery than streaming. 

  • Turn the display brightness down - If your model has a this setting in the Yoto App, choose a lower setting, especially overnight.




Checking the battery level


The quickest way: a short press of the power button (with your player switched on, no card in and not on charge) shows the battery level on the display.


Your player also shows its battery level by itself when you:

  • Take it off the wireless charging dock - Yoto Player (3rd and 4th Generation). Give it about 10 seconds to update.

  • Unplug the charging cable - Yoto Player (3rd and 4th Generation) and Yoto Mini.

  • Short-press the power button while it’s switched off and charging - Yoto Player (3rd and 4th Generation).

  • Take it off its charging dock - Yoto Player (2nd Generation only).

Prefer the app? Whichever model you have, you'll find the battery level in the Settings tab of the Yoto App, if you scroll down to Status.


Waiting for "fully charged"? The indicator needs the player to be switched on and charging for about 30 seconds before it shows as fully charged. If it is charged while switched off, turn it on, wait half a minute, then check.


Good to know - low battery and volume

When the Yoto player (3rd and 4th Generations) battery is getting low, the volume is automatically limited to maintain optimal system performance. The volume bar will show as solid red when you reach the volume limit.


Related help: How long does the battery take to charge?; How to charge your Yoto player.

articles.title: Using the Yoto App on iOS and Android
articles.body:
Getting started with the Yoto app

If you are a brand-new user, choose Set up your player from either the landing screen or the Settings section.

As a second parent or family member with a player that has already been set up, choose Join a Family Account (from either the landing screen or the Settings section of the app).

 



News tab

This is where you can see up-to-date news from Yoto, tips on how to use your player and articles on things we find interesting, and hopefully you may too.


Create tab


This is the hub of Create in the app. Here you'll be able to:

  • Record yourself narrating a story
  • Access your previous recordings
  • Make a playlist with your recordings or from mp3s
  • Discover content from other creators on our community site: https://yoto.space
  • Access how to Make Your Own guides to help you to create your own content


Library tab

The library is the heart of the app. 

From here, you can:

  • See (and play) all the cards you own
  • See (and play) all Make Your Own playlists that you have created or that have been shared with you
  • See (and play) all free cards (radio, podcasts, sleep etc.) you've added to your library
  • See (and play) all Club Collection cards you've added to your library
  • See and remotely control what's playing on a player


To play any of the content in the app, click the play icon, located on the image of that audio, and it will automatically play on the player or phone selected.

The Device Picker (above the main tab navigation and now playing info) allows you to select which device you are controlling, and playing audio on. 

The Now Playing area shows you which piece of content you are playing on your phone, and allows you to pause or resume playing. Tapping on the Now Playing area opens up the Maxi Player. From here you can skip chapters or tracks and adjust the volume. 

From the Maxi Player, you can also: 

  • Set a sleep timer by tapping on the moon and stars icon in the right-hand corner.
  • Choose the playback speed, rewind/ forward within the chapter by 15 seconds or by using the slider at the top.
  • See the chapters of a card by pressing on the burger menu..

 

Discover tab

This is where you'll find and discover all of our free content covering radio, podcasts, sleep and stories. You can play all content from here and if you like it, you can add it to your own library for fast access. Just tap on the content to see the content details and tap 'Add to library'.


Settings tab


This is where you can see details of who is in your Family Account and all of your players.

Your registered details are at the top of the screen (this is the email address you used to sign in to the app). You will also be able to see details of all users (including you) in your Family Account who are paired with your players.

Under the list of users, you will also see all the players linked to your Family Account. 

Each listed player has a chevron icon. Tap this icon to manage settings for that player. 


STATUS

Player name - Personalize your player by giving it a name

Battery level - view battery level of your player

Manage Wi-Fi - disconnect your player from the Wi-Fi or add a new network

Audio Download Status - This shows you if all your cards have been downloaded to your player, or if some content still needs to download. If content is not downloaded fully, it will need to stream, which may cause playback issues if you have poor Wi-Fi in the location of your player


ALARMS

Set-up up to 10 alarms. 


DAY AND NIGHT MODE

Morning - Set a start time for day mode (the clock will change from moon to sun)

Bedtime - Set a start time for night mode (your clock will change from sun to moon)

Morning Light / Nightlight Color (V2/V3 only) - Choose the color of the light on the rear of the Player. You can set different colors for night and day, so your child knows when it’s time to get up, even if the player is on its front. Only for Yoto Player: the Yoto Mini does not have a night light.

Auto Display Brightness (V3 only) - Enable the Display Brightness to be auto-adjusted based on ambient light.

Display Brightness - Set the default screen brightness during day/night modes when Auto Display Brightness is disabled/unavailable.

Volume Limit - Set a limit for how loud your player will go for the day/night modes.

Note: this volume limit applies to the Speaker and Wired Headphone outputs. The Yoto Wireless Headphones feature their own kid-safe volume limiting.

Right Button Shortcuts - By default, your player will play Yoto Daily and Yoto Radio on first and second press during the day; and Yoto Sleep Radio on first press during the night. These can be edited to include French Language items and Timers. 


ADVANCED

Battery saver - Set how quickly the player display dims when no buttons or cards are touched, and when not on the dock. 

Auto Power-Off - Set how quickly the player switched off when no buttons or cards are touched while off charge. 

Bluetooth pairing - Toggle this on to allow your player to enter Bluetooth mode, so you can play audio through your player just like any other Bluetooth speaker.

Be aware, toggling this one does not turn on Bluetooth mode, it unlocks the feature, so you can subsequently enter Bluetooth mode by pressing the left-hand orange button for 3 seconds. 

Headphone volume limit - set up a volume limit when audio is played with headphone.

24-hour clock - Choose between a 12 and 24-hour clock for the front display of your player.

Automatic time zone - Ensure the time zone for your clock is set correctly (includes updates for daylight saving).

Yoto OS version - See which software version your player is on.

Yoto App version - See which software version your app is on.

Registration code - The six-letter code you used to set up your player. It is used to troubleshoot issues, if you have them.

Player MAC Address 

Yoto Beta labs - to join our beta user.

Unpair this player from Family Account - to unpair a player from your account.

articles.body:
When nothing is playing and the clock is showing, press the Green Button to play the first item on the Green Button menu (default set to Yoto Daily). 


Every player keeps it simple: turn, press, or hold. Find your model below for exactly what each button does.


Not sure where to look at? See: Which Yoto do I have?


4th Generation controls


Left orange button

  • Turn to adjust the volume.

  • Short press to skip to the previous track.

  • Press and hold to rewind.

  • When the clock is showing, press and hold to pair Bluetooth headphones.



Right orange button

  • Turn to navigate through tracks, then press to select one.

  • Short press to skip to the next track.

  • Press and hold to fast-forward.



The Green Button

  • Twist to browse your child’s favourites - the artwork appears on the display - then press to play.

  • When nothing is playing and the clock is showing, press the Green Button to play the first item on the Green Button menu (default set to Yoto Daily).

Earlier players controls

articles.title: Does my Yoto need to be online to play content?
articles.body:
Only twice: when you first set it up, and the first time you play each card. Once a card has downloaded, it plays anywhere - car, campsite, Grandma’s - no internet needed.

The exception - audio that needs to be streamed over Wi-Fi by nature, like radio stations and podcasts, always needs your player to be online.


When your player needs to be online


  • Setting up:  your player connects to Wi-Fi as part of setup. 
  • The first play of any card: the audio streams from our servers while your player downloads it in the background, so you’ll need a solid connection.
  • Radio stations and podcasts: cards linked to these stream continuously, so they won’t play offline.
  • Playing to your player from the app: both your phone and your player need to be online.


When your player does not need to be online


  • Any card that’s finished downloading plays straight from your player’s built-in storage - completely offline.

On your phone, it’s simpler still: if your phone has internet (Wi-Fi or mobile data), the app can play anything in your library, including radio, podcasts and cards that haven’t downloaded to the player yet.


How do I download audio before a trip?


First, connect your player to Wi-Fi and plug it in to charge. You can check its connection in the Yoto App.

To start downloading audio:

  • On any Yoto Player or Yoto Mini: Insert each Yoto Card and let it play for a few seconds.

  • On a Yoto Player 4th Gen or Yoto Mini 4th Gen: You can also download titles that are already in your Yoto Library by adding them to a Green Button playlist. Some titles purchased as physical cards will only appear in your Library after you’ve inserted the card once. [Learn how to use the Green Button.]

Once you’ve added your Green Button titles or played each card for a few seconds, remove any card and leave the player switched on, plugged in and idle while the downloads complete. Leaving it overnight before a trip works a treat.

To check your downloads, open the Yoto App, go to Settings, select your player and tap Audio Download Status. You’ll see which titles have downloaded and which are still waiting.


Got more than one Yoto player?


All the cards in your library download to each of your players:

  • If your library fits within a player’s storage, everything downloads.

  • If your library is bigger than a player’s storage, the least-played cards make room for the most popular ones, worked out per player. Nothing leaves your app library, and any card re-downloads when you play it online. 


Related help: How much audio can my Yoto player store?; Playing your first Yoto Card.

articles.title: How much content can my Yoto store for offline listening?
articles.body:
Plenty! Every Yoto player stores hundreds of hours of audio for offline listening, and when it’s full, your player quietly makes room by itself. Everything always stays safe in your Yoto App library. 


How much audio can my Yoto player store for offline listening? 


Storage capacity depends on the model you own. 

Not sure where to look? See: Which Yoto do I have?

Yoto model

Built-in storage

Estimated audio capacity* 

Yoto Player and Yoto Mini (4th Generation)

64 GB

At least 1,000 hours

Yoto Player (3rd Generation)

32 GB

Around 700 hours

Yoto Mini (2024 Edition) and Yoto Mini (2021–2023 Edition)

16 GB or 32 GB - one quick check below

Around 250 or 700 hours

Yoto Player (2nd Generation)

16GB 

Around 350 hours

*Estimates based on spoken-word audio, like Roald Dahl or Julia Donaldson stories. Music may take up more space, so a music-heavy library may store fewer hours


Check the storage on an earlier Yoto Mini 

Turn it over and look at the serial number on the base:

  • 16 GB - the serial number starts with 5 or a lower number, and doesn't end in -H, -H7 or -U.

  • 32 GB - everything else (starts with 6 or higher, starts with letters, or ends in -H, -H7 or -U).


When the storage is full

Nothing you’ll notice - and don’t worry, it won’t be “lost” from your library: 

  • Your player automatically removes the audio that hasn’t been played for the longest time, to make room for new downloads of more popular content. 

  • Removed audio stays in your Yoto App library. To get it back on the player, just play it while your Yoto is online, it downloads again automatically.


Check storage and downloads

In the Yoto App, go to Settings, select your player and open Audio Download Status. If your model does not show a storage total, use the title list to check which audio is ready offline.

articles.title: Using your Yoto as a nightlight
articles.body:
Turn your Yoto Player onto its front, and the nightlight comes on. Stand it upright, and it’s off. But there’s a little more to it… 

One quick tip: flip it on a hard, flat surface like a bedside table. Avoid carpeted floors or beds.



Adjusting the brightness

While the player is face down, twist the right-hand orange dial - left to dim (all the way down to off), right to brighten.

Yoto Player (4th Generation) adjusts itself: its auto-brightness dims the nightlight to match the light in the room. Twisting the dial overrides it for the night - stand the player upright and pop it back down, and auto-brightness takes over again.


Changing the colour

Pick your nightlight colour in the Yoto App: go to the Settings tab and tap the arrow icon next to your player.

You can set a different colour for Day and Night mode - a lovely okay-to-wake cue for little ones who can’t read the clock yet: one colour means it’s still sleep time, another means it’s fine to get up. 



While the nightlight is on - Yoto Player (4th Generation)

The display switches off so it doesn’t light up the room. Your child can still:

  • Play and pause audio

  • Change the volume

  • Skip through tracks

Please also note that selecting content on the Green Button is disabled when the nightlight is on.


Good to know

  • Yoto Player (3rd Generation): the room-temperature sensor takes a break while the player is in nightlight mode.

  • Yoto Mini does not have a nightlight, but it does have a Day and Night mode! 


Related help: How to control your Yoto player.

articles.title: What do the icons on my Yoto display mean?
articles.body:
Your Yoto player uses little pixel icons to tell you what it’s up to. Find the icon you can see below - each one comes with what it means and what to do next, if anything.


The same icons appear on Yoto Player and Yoto Mini. However, 4th Generation players have a fresh new icon set, so there are two icon columns: check the one that matches your player. 

Not sure where to look at? See: Which Yoto do I have? (article redirection) 


Wi-Fi and Set up

4 Generation

Earlier players


What it means - and what to do


White Yoto face:

Your player is offline and doesn’t know the time yet. Run setup in the Yoto App to get it online.


White Wi-Fi waves:

(animated) Your player is connecting to Wi-Fi. Just give it a moment.

Waves with a green tick / Green waves:

Connected! 


(static) Wi-Fi setup was successful. 

(animated) Green waves animating means a software update is in progress - leave the player on and connected.

Waves with a red mark / red cross: 

The Wi-Fi connection or setup didn’t work. Try again. If it keeps happening, see: Wi-Fi and connection troubleshooting.



Card with a red arrow pointing up: 

Remove the card so setup can begin.


Battery and charging 

4 Generation

Earlier players

What it means - and what to do


Blue battery with a lightning bolt: 

Charging away - nothing to do.

Green battery: 

The battery level is good.


Red battery with a line through it: 

The battery is too low for the player to turn on. Leave it on charge for a while, then try again.



Red battery:

Very low - your player will switch off soon unless you pop it on charge. 



Yellow battery with an exclamation mark:

A battery fault has been detected and the player will switch itself off. Please contact us if you see this one.


Yoto Mini with a charging cable and yellow exclamation mark: 

A battery fault has been detected - unplug the charging cable so the player can shut down safely, then contact us.


Player with a charging cable and a water droplet:

Liquid detected.  Let the device dry fully first and check out 

 


Cards and Playback

4 Generation

Earlier players


What it means - and what to do


Loading / Circle of Dots: 

Your update, audio or its artwork is still loading or downloading. Give it a moment - staying online helps it finish faster.For 4th Gen, the loader is spinning



Blue cloud over an icon:

This audio is streaming rather than playing from the player - it hasn’t downloaded yet, so it needs the internet to keep playing. 

Card with a blue cloud and green waves:

The player is offline and this card’s audio hasn’t been downloaded. Connect to Wi-Fi to play it the first time. 


Red stop sign over a card: 

wasn’t recognised. Take it out and try again. Still no luck? See:  



Exclamation mark over a card:

There has been a problem playing this audio. Try again and if it still doesn’t work please contact Customer Happiness.


“Yoto App” on the display / With an arrow pointing down:

On 3rd Gen and older this shows when you try and put a card in before you've set up the Player. 

O 4th Gen, the new animated icon shows straight out of the box without any interaction prompts. 



Red cross while play:

Either the Wi-Fi setup process has failed, or linking content to a MYO card has failed. 



Card with a red arrow pointing up: 

Remove the card so setup can begin.

Red volume line:

The volume can’t go any higher because a volume limit is set to zero. You can adjust limits in the Yoto App. 


Blue Yoto face:

The artwork for this audio couldn’t load - it’s incompatible, it has no artwork attached or the connection dropped while streaming. It will still play as normal. 



Bluetooth and headphones

4 Generation

Earlier players


What it means - and what to do



Grey headphones with blue Bluetooth symbol: 

Pairing with your headphones - keep them close and in pairing mode. 



Coloured headphones with a green tick and a single blue pixel: 

Headphones successfully paired! Audio now plays through the headphones.



Grey headphones with a red exclamation mark / Grey Bluetooth logo with red cross:

Pairing failed or timed out - or you left the Bluetooth menu before finishing. Put your headphones back into pairing mode and try again.


Grey headphones with a grey Bluetooth symbol:

Headphones unpaired - the player has switched back to its own speaker.


Clock 


Sun or Moon with Red time:

 The daytime/nightime clock is shown when nothing is playing. If the time is Red, it means your player is online.

Sun or Moon with White time: 

Same as above, but if the time is white, it means your player is offline. 




Other errors

ERR followed by digits:

If your Yoto player display shows "ERR" followed by a three digits number (for example, "ERR 184") it can indicate different internal issues (potentially more than one issue) with your device. Please contact us if you see this.

ERR BRK:

If your Yoto Mini display shows "ERRBRK", we have detected a battery issue that needs attention. To ensure your player remains safe to use, please request your free battery replacement kit. Click here for more information on the battery replacement kit.



Seeing something that isn’t here?

Contact our Customer Happiness team with your player model and a photo or description of what’s on the display - we’ll tell you exactly what it means. 

The same icons appear on Yoto Player and Yoto Mini. However, 4th Generation players have a fresh new icon set, so there are two icon columns: check the one that matches your player. 

Not sure where to look at? See: Which Yoto do I have?

articles.title: Which Yoto player do I have?
articles.body:
Grab your player; this takes less than a minute. Once you’ve matched yours, use the same model name wherever it appears in our guides.

Choose your device

  • Yoto Player: The larger, cube-shaped device. 

  • Yoto Mini:  The smaller, portable device with a carry loop or lanyard.


Yoto Player models

Yoto Player (4th Generation) 

Quickest clue: the Green Button on the right-hand side, no earlier Yoto Player has one.

  • Power button: Bottom-right corner.

  • Charging: USB-C or wireless charging.

  • At the base of the Player: Look for “Model: YP5” near the bottom.


Yoto Player (3rd Generation) 


Quickest clue: a small grey power button on the right side, with a USB-C port below it.

  • Power button: Right-hand side, near the middle.

  • Charging: USB-C or wireless charging.

  • At the base of the Player: Look for “Model: YP004” near the bottom. Also, the barcode is wide, nothing like a QR code.


Yoto Player (2nd Generation)

Quickest clue: the front face is flat and does not have the raised border found around the 3rd Generation display.

  • Power button: On the bottom-right corner of the Player.

  • Charging: It has no USB-C port and charges only through its dedicated magnetic charging dock.

  • Serial Numbers: Look at the base of the player, you'll find “P2” somewhere near the middle of the serial number. 


Yoto Mini models

Yoto Mini (4th Generation)

Quickest clue:  the Green Button on the right-hand side, no earlier Yoto Mini has one.

  • Power button: Top-right corner.

  • Charging: USB-C.

  • Serial number: Look at the base of the player, you'll find “M3” somewhere near the middle of the serial number, which is split over two lines.


Yoto Mini (2024 Edition) and Yoto Mini (2021–2023 Edition)


These two editions look identical and both have:

  • Two orange dials at the top of the front

  • A speaker on the left

  • A small display on the right

The serial number on the base is the way to tell them apart:


Your serial number…

Your model

Ends with -H, -H7 or -U (however it starts)

Yoto Mini (2024 Edition)

Starts with 9FE, or AFE, BFE, CFE… (continuing down the alphabet), or AVC, BVC, CVC… (continuing down the alphabet)

Yoto Mini (2024 Edition)

Starts with 1FE to 8FE and doesn’t end in -H, -H7 or -U

Yoto Mini (2021–2023 Edition)


Good to know: the Yoto Mini (2021–2023 Edition) is covered by the Yoto Mini Battery Replacement Kit programme. You can check if your Yoto Mini is affected here. 


Still not sure? 

No worries. Start a chat with our Customer Happiness team and share a photo of the base of your player. We’ll identify it for you in no time.

articles.title: Can I change my account's email address?
articles.body:
The email address of your Yoto account cannot be changed.

If you have lost access to your old email address, please create a new Yoto account. By adding your new Yoto account to the Family Account, you will retain access to your devices and library.

The order history, wish list, saved address, and Yoto Club subscriptions, however, cannot be moved — but we can do our best to help you close down the old account. If you need help, please get in touch.
